items.title: Check in at 57 Myeongdong Hostel
items.fixed: From Incheon: the airport limousine bus (6015 to Myeongdong, ≈70–90 min, ≈₩17k pp) is the easy choice with bags — it drops you two minutes from the hostel. AREX + Line 4 is cheaper but means stairs and a change; a taxi is ≈₩70–80k.
tips: Arriving early? Leave the bags at reception.
Buy a T-money card (₩4,000 + top-up) at the first convenience store you see.
Nearest metro: Myeongdong (Line 4) exit 8.

items.title: Namsan Cable Car
items.name: Namsan Cable Car
items.about: A 605 m aerial tramway running since 1962 that lifts you from the edge of Myeongdong to the top of Namsan in about three minutes.
items.fixed: Walk ≈10 min uphill from the hostel (Sopa-ro), or take the free glass elevator from Hoehyeon to the lower station.
items.need: 3 min ride · queue 20–60 min near sunset
tips: Be in line by 16:30 — the queue balloons before sunset.
Stand on the right side going up for the city view.
Buy a return: the walk down is 30 min in the dark.

items.title: N Seoul Tower & love locks
items.name: N Seoul Tower
items.about: Seoul's landmark broadcast tower on the 243 m Namsan peak. The open terrace and the fences of love locks are free; the observatory sits 236 m above the mountain.
items.fixed: Cable car + a 5 min walk up to the plaza.
tips: Bring a padlock from a stationery shop (≈₩3,000); on the terrace they cost more.
Be up by 17:00 for the blue hour, stay until the city lights come on.
The tower's colour shows the air quality — blue means clean.

items.title: Dinner after the tower
items.fixed: Ride the cable car back down (last car 23:00). Donkatsu 101 is 3 min from the lower station; Myeongdong Kyoja and the street stalls are a 10–12 min walk downhill; Euljiro's Nogari Alley is 15 min on foot or a 5-min taxi.

options.title: Namsan Donkatsu 101
options.name: 101번지남산돈까스
options.about: Namsan's famous wang-donkkaseu — a plate-sized, thin, crisp cutlet in sweet brown sauce — right below the cable-car station. Seoul taxi drivers have eaten here for 30 years.
options.cool: The original of the Namsan cutlet houses; huge portions, pickled radish refills.
options.booking: No reservations; short queue on weekends.
tips: One cutlet each is more than enough; share a side of udon.
Card accepted.

options.title: Myeongdong Kyoja
options.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
options.about: Knife-cut noodles in a rich chicken broth and plump dumplings — a Michelin Bib Gourmand institution since 1966, famous for its fiercely garlicky kimchi.
options.cool: Only four dishes on the menu; the kimchi is legendary.
options.booking: No reservations, fast turnover — 10–20 min queue at peak.
tips: Kalguksu ₩11k, mandu ₩13k — split both.
Two branches 100 m apart; the smaller one has shorter lines.

options.title: Myeongdong street food
options.name: 명동거리
options.about: Korea's busiest shopping street turns into an open-air food market at night. Graze from stall to stall.
options.cool: Tornado potato, tteokbokki, egg bread (gyeranppang), hotteok, grilled cheese lobster if you're feeling flush.
tips: Skip the ₩15k lobster tails if you're watching the budget.
Cards work at most stalls; cash is quicker.

options.title: Euljiro Nogari Alley
options.type: Korean pub food · dried pollack & draught beer
options.name: 을지로 노가리골목
options.about: An alley of 1980s beer halls where the whole street sits at plastic tables over grilled dried pollack (nogari, ₩1–2k each) and cheap draught beer — 'Hip-jiro' at its most retro.
options.cool: Manseon Hof is the original; the street itself is a registered 'Seoul Future Heritage'.
tips: Order nogari + a plate of fried chicken gizzards or golbaengi to share.
Drinks are extra: draught ≈₩4k.

items.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace
items.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
items.about: The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty (1395), restored after its demolition under Japanese rule. Grand halls, pavilion ponds and a mountain backdrop — the postcard image of Seoul.
items.metro: Line 4 Myeongdong → Chungmuro, Line 3 → Gyeongbokgung (exit 5), ≈20 min.
tips: Royal guard changing at 10:00 at Gwanghwamun gate — arrive by 09:50.
Free English tours at 11:00 and 13:30 from the info centre.
Photo spots: Gyeonghoeru pavilion pond, Hyangwonjeong.

items.title: National Folk Museum of Korea
items.name: National Folk Museum of Korea
items.about: Inside the palace grounds: three galleries on how Koreans lived, worked and celebrated for the last 600 years, plus an open-air street of 1970s shopfronts.
tips: Enter from inside Gyeongbokgung — no extra ticket.
The outdoor 'Street of Memories' is a fun quick photo stop.

options.title: Tosokchon Samgyetang
options.name: Tosokchon Samgyetang
options.about: A whole young chicken stuffed with rice, ginseng, jujube and garlic, simmered in a hanok courtyard restaurant that presidents have eaten in.
options.cool: The most famous samgyetang in Seoul; comes with a shot of ginseng liquor.
options.booking: No reservations; 15–30 min queue at lunch — arrive by 12:15.
tips: One bowl each (₩20k); the black-chicken version is ₩5k more.
Gyeongbokgung station exit 2, 5 min west of the palace.

options.title: Samcheongdong Sujebi
options.name: 삼청동수제비
options.about: A 40-year institution on the Samcheong-dong lane: chewy hand-torn dough in an anchovy-clam broth, with a giant kimchi pancake to share.
options.cool: Cash-only feel, tiny tables, exactly two things worth ordering.
tips: Sujebi ≈₩9k each + one kimchi-jeon (₩12k) between you.
10 min walk north from the museum along the palace wall.

options.title: Pottery-painting class in Bukchon
options.name: 북촌 도자기 페인팅 공방
options.about: Paint your own cups or plates in a small hanok studio; pieces are glazed and fired and can be collected in a few days or shipped.
options.cool: You leave with matching cups you made together.
options.booking: Book a 14:00 slot a few days ahead via Naver or Klook; several studios sit around Bukchon-ro and Gye-dong.
tips: Ask about pick-up before Nov 6, or shipping to your last hotel.
Wear nothing precious — glaze stains.

options.title: Wander the Bukchon lanes
options.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
options.about: A 600-year-old neighbourhood of hanok (traditional wooden houses) on the hill between the two palaces, still home to Seoulites.
options.cool: Bukchon-ro 11-gil: tiled roofs with the skyline behind them.
options.hours: Visitor hours 10:00–17:00 · residential lanes closed Sundays
tips: People live here: quiet voices, no music.
Fines apply in restricted lanes outside visitor hours.

options.title: Insadong tea house & Ssamziegil
options.name: Ssamziegil, Insadong
options.about: Seoul's traditional arts street: antique shops, galleries, teahouses and the spiralling Ssamziegil craft arcade.
options.cool: Order omija (five-flavour berry) or yuja tea in a traditional teahouse.
tips: Good gifts: hanji paper, ceramics, tea.
Shin Old Tea House hides in an alley off the main street.

options.title: Jogyesa Temple
options.name: Jogyesa Temple
options.about: Head temple of Korean Buddhism's Jogye Order, hidden behind Insadong: a 500-year-old white pine, a main hall with three huge golden Buddhas, and thousands of hanging lanterns.
options.cool: Chrysanthemum festival displays usually fill the courtyard in late October / early November.
tips: Take your shoes off to sit inside the hall for a few minutes.
Two minutes from Insadong's main street.

options.title: Koong — Gaeseong dumplings
options.name: 궁 인사동
options.about: Fist-sized Gaeseong-style dumplings, dumpling soup and pyeonsu (square summer dumplings) from a family recipe that's been served in Insadong for over 40 years.
options.cool: Michelin Bib Gourmand; the dumplings are hand-pleated in the window.
tips: Mandu-guk (₩14k) + a plate of steamed mandu (₩15k) to share.
Five minutes from Ssamziegil and Jogyesa.

options.title: Woo Lae Oak — cold noodles only
options.name: Woo Lae Oak
options.about: Seoul's most storied restaurant (1946): delicate Pyongyang-style buckwheat noodles in a clear, cold beef broth, served in a grand old dining room.
options.cool: The naengmyeon that Seoul food critics measure all others by.
options.booking: No reservations; queue at 18:00 is short. Closed Mondays.
tips: Budget tip: order naengmyeon only (≈₩17k) — the bulgogi is ₩50k+.
Euljiro 4-ga station exit 4; taxi 7 min from Insadong.

options.title: Moonlight Lotus Show at Changgyeonggung
options.name: Changgyeonggung Palace
options.about: An evening of light on the palace's lotus pond (Chundangji) and the Victorian glasshouse — reserved-entry sessions with the whole palace lit after dark.
tips: Foreigners book via Creatrip — the Korean sites need a Korean phone number.
Enter through Honghwamun, the main gate on Changgyeonggung-ro.
Taxi back to Myeongdong ≈15 min, ≈₩9k.
options.cool: The lotus pond and the 1909 glasshouse lit from the water; almost silent.
options.booking: Reserved sessions 19:00 / 19:30 / 20:00 — foreigners book via Creatrip.

options.title: Cheonggyecheon by night & Gwanghwamun
options.name: 청계광장
options.about: The sunken stream lit after dark from Cheonggye Plaza east, then up to Gwanghwamun Square with the palace gate and the mountains floodlit behind it.
options.cool: Candle-lit waterfall at the plaza; the lantern festival sometimes runs here in early November.
tips: Start at Cheonggye Plaza (Line 5 Gwanghwamun exit 5) and walk 20 min east, then back.
Ten minutes on foot to Myeongdong afterwards.

options.title: Jongno 3-ga pocha street
options.name: 종로3가 포차거리
options.about: After 19:00 the lane behind Jongno 3-ga station fills with orange tents and plastic stools: grilled clams, eomuk, soju and the whole city's office crowd.
options.cool: The most Seoul night out there is, for the price of two drinks.
options.booking: None — sit wherever there's a stool.
tips: Order one dish per tent and move along.
Line 1/3/5 Jongno 3-ga, exit 6.

options.title: Hadongkwan — gomtang
options.name: Hadongkwan Myeongdong
options.about: Since 1939: a bowl of clear beef-and-tripe soup over rice, seasoned at the table with salt and spring onion. Seoul's classic morning-after breakfast.
options.cool: They close when the broth runs out — often by mid-afternoon.
tips: 'Botong' (regular, ≈₩18k) is plenty; add kimchi juice to the broth like the regulars.
Two minutes from the hostel.

options.title: Myeongdong Kyoja
options.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
options.about: Knife-cut noodles in chicken broth and plump dumplings at the 1966 Bib Gourmand institution — quiet and quick at 10:30.
options.cool: The garlic kimchi is legendary.
tips: Kalguksu ₩11k, mandu ₩13k — split both.

options.title: Namsangol Hanok Village
options.name: Namsangol Hanok Village
options.about: Five restored aristocratic hanok moved here from around Seoul, set in a traditional garden at the foot of Namsan with a time capsule buried for the year 2394.
options.cool: Quiet courtyards, free traditional-games corner, autumn colour in the garden.
tips: Chungmuro station exit 3–4.
Free tea ceremony demos some afternoons.

options.title: Myeongdong shopping & K-beauty
options.name: Myeongdong Street
options.about: Olive Young's flagship, Innisfree, Etude and every K-beauty brand within four blocks — quieter before noon.
options.cool: Tax refund at the counter for purchases over ₩15k with your passport.
tips: Sheet masks make light gifts.
Skip the tourist-trap cosmetics touts on the main drag.

items.title: Deoksugung Palace & stone-wall road
items.name: Deoksugung Palace
items.about: The smallest of Seoul's palaces mixes Korean halls with early-20th-century Western buildings; the stone-wall road outside is the city's most famous autumn walk.
tips: Guard ceremony at Daehanmun gate 11:00, 14:00, 15:30.
Local legend says couples who walk the stone-wall road break up — hold hands and ignore it.
Ginkgo trees on Doldam-gil turn gold at the end of October.

items.title: Yeouido Hangang Park
items.name: Yeouido Hangang Park
items.about: The busiest stretch of the Han River park, on the island that holds the National Assembly — grass, bike paths and the riverside promenade.
items.metro: Metro: Line 2 City Hall → Chungjeongno, Line 5 → Yeouinaru (exit 2–3), ≈25 min.
tips: Tandem bikes rent for ≈₩10,000/h.
The cruise pier is a 5-min walk from the station.

options.title: Sunset Han River cruise
options.name: 이랜드크루즈 여의도
options.about: Cruises leave the Yeouido pier and loop under the bridges — at sunset you get the 63 Building, Namsan and the bridge lights all at once.
tips: Book the sailing closest to the 17:38 sunset.
The open upper deck is cold in November — bring a layer.
options.cool: The 63 Building, Namsan and the bridge lights from the water.
options.booking: Book the sailing closest to the 17:38 sunset a week ahead.

options.title: Banpo Bridge Moonlight Rainbow Fountain
options.name: 반포대교 달빛무지개분수
options.about: The longest bridge fountain in the world: 380 jets along both sides of Banpo Bridge, lit in colour and set to music, watched from the grass of Banpo Hangang Park.
options.cool: Late October is the very end of the season — the last shows of the year.
options.booking: None. Evening shows usually 20:00, 20:30, 21:00 (20 min each); check the Hangang park site for the day.
tips: Taxi ≈15 min from Yeouido (≈₩10k) or Line 9 to Sinbanggyo.
Eat first on Yeouido — the fountain is a show, not a dinner spot.

options.title: River ramyeon at the convenience store
options.name: CU 여의나루역점
options.about: Cooking instant noodles at a Han River convenience store is a Seoul rite of passage — cheap, warm and strangely romantic.
options.cool: Self-cook ramyeon machines, riverside tables, bridge lights.
tips: Add a triangle kimbap and a can of Cass — that's the date.
Taxi back to Myeongdong ≈20 min, ≈₩15k.

options.title: The Hyundai Seoul — B1 food hall
options.name: The Hyundai Seoul
options.about: Seoul's most beautiful department store: an indoor forest under a glass roof, and a basement food hall of Seoul's trendiest bakeries, ramen, gimbap and dessert counters.
options.cool: Sounds Forest on the 5th floor is worth the escalator ride before you eat.
options.booking: None; food hall open till 20:30 on Fridays.
tips: Five minutes' walk west from Yeouinaru; pick two counters and share.
Taxi home ≈20 min, or Line 5 → Line 2 back to Euljiro.

title: Move to Seongsu, drones over the river

items.title: Check out, drop bags at Haru Forest
items.metro: Metro: Line 2 Euljiro 1-ga → Konkuk Univ. (≈20 min, 8 stops), or a taxi ≈25 min.
tips: Korean listings show overnight check-in 20:00 / checkout 13:00 — confirm check-in and drop the bags at 11:30.
Konkuk Univ. station (Lines 2 & 7) is 5 min from the hotel.

options.title: Seongsu Jokbal
options.name: 성수족발
options.about: Seongsu's landmark for 40 years: soy-braised trotters sliced thin, wrapped in lettuce with garlic and salted shrimp sauce.
options.cool: Order the 'half-half' — original and spicy — with a bowl of cold bean-sprout soup.
tips: A medium (≈₩40k) feeds two comfortably.
Seongsu station exit 4.

options.title: Cafe Onion Seongsu
options.name: Cafe Onion Seongsu
options.about: A bombed-out 1970s factory turned into Seoul's most photographed bakery: raw concrete, an open courtyard and trays of pandoro dusted with sugar.
options.cool: The pandoro 'snow mountain' pastry and the rooftop.
options.booking: None; weekends queue at the counter.
tips: Two pastries + two coffees ≈₩25k total.
Seongsu station exit 2, 3 min.

options.title: Perfume-making workshop
options.name: 성수 향수공방
options.about: Blend your own 50 ml fragrance from 40-odd notes with a perfumer's guidance in one of the studios around Seongsu station — you each leave with a bottle named by the other.
options.cool: A very Seoul date; the bottles make the best souvenir.
options.booking: Book a 14:30 Saturday slot 1–2 weeks ahead via Naver or Klook.
tips: Most studios speak enough English; Klook listings are in English.
Bottles are liquid — pack them in checked luggage.

options.title: Han River bike ride on Seoul Bike
options.name: 뚝섬한강공원 따릉이 대여소
options.about: Rent the green city bikes (Ttareungyi) and ride the riverside path from Ttukseom to Jamsil Bridge and back — flat, car-free and golden in late October.
options.cool: The path passes under Cheongdam Bridge with the Lotte Tower ahead.
options.booking: None; register in the Seoul Bike app with a foreign card.
tips: Return to any dock; 1-hour passes can be renewed.
Helmets are not provided — ride slowly.

items.title: Seoul Forest
items.name: Seoul Forest Park
items.about: A 1.2 km² park on a former racecourse — wetlands, a deer enclosure and, at the end of October, an avenue of gold ginkgo.
tips: Deer park and the ginkgo path are near the main gate.
A footbridge over the tracks leads on to the river park.

items.title: Picnic at Ttukseom: chicken & beer
items.name: Ttukseom Hangang Park
items.about: Riverside park with delivery zones and picnic mats for rent — where Seoulites do chimaek (chicken and beer) on the grass. Tonight the sky show is here too.
tips: Order from a delivery kiosk or app and give them your pillar number.
Halloween night: avoid Itaewon and Hongdae — the river is the right place to be.
Mats rent for ≈₩5k; bring a layer, it's cold by the water.

items.title: Hangang Drone Light Show — Marvel finale
items.name: 뚝섬한강공원 드론라이트쇼
items.about: The season finale of Seoul's Hangang drone light show: 2,000 drones over the river in a Marvel-themed programme, 19:30–21:25 with the main show around 20:30.
items.fixed: You're already there — stay on the grass with a view over the water. Afterwards, walk home ≈25 min along Ttukseom-ro to the hotel (or a 7-min taxi).
tips: Sat 31 Oct is the finale — expect crowds; claim your spot by 19:00.
Walk home ≈25 min; taxis are scarce right after the show.

options.title: Sleep in
options.name: 하루포레스트호텔 성수&건대점
options.about: No alarm. Coffee from the convenience store, a lie-in, and out by noon.
options.cool: It's Sunday.

options.title: Korean sauna at Siloam Sauna, Junggok-dong
options.name: 실로암사우나 중곡동
options.about: A basic neighbourhood Korean bathhouse: hot and cold pools, a dry sauna and a scrub station, with separate men's and women's baths.
options.cool: The real, unglamorous Korean Sunday-morning ritual.
options.booking: None; entry fee at the desk includes towels and clothes.
tips: Baths are naked and gender-separated; meet again in the mixed jjimjil room in the sauna clothes.
Taxi ≈10 min from the hotel.

options.title: Common Ground
options.name: Common Ground
options.about: Two hundred blue shipping containers stacked into a mall of small brands, with a food terrace of burgers, pasta and Korean bowls on the top deck.
options.cool: Sunday market stalls in the courtyard.
tips: Five minutes' walk from the hotel.
Good coffee at the ground-floor cafés.

options.title: Cafe Onion Seongsu
options.name: Cafe Onion Seongsu
options.about: The factory-turned-bakery of Seongsu; if you missed it yesterday, Sunday brunch here is the move.
options.cool: Pandoro pastry and the courtyard.
options.booking: None; queue at the counter on Sundays.
tips: Two pastries + two coffees ≈₩25k total.

options.title: Seokchon Lake Park
options.name: Seokchon Lake Park
options.about: Two lakes ringed by a promenade in Songpa, with Lotte World's castle on one side and the 555 m tower above everything.
options.cool: Cherry trees turning red in early November.
options.metro: Line 2 Konkuk Univ. → Jamsil, 4 stops (≈10 min), exit 2–3.
tips: Walk the east lake, then the tower is a 5-min stroll.

options.title: Olympic Park lone tree
options.name: 올림픽공원 나홀로나무
options.about: A single tree on a vast lawn inside the 1988 Olympic Park — Seoul's favourite couple-photo spot, ringed by the ancient earthen Mongchon fortress.
options.cool: Wild-flower hill and the fortress walk if you have energy.
options.metro: Line 2 → Jamsil, Line 8 → Mongchontoseong (exit 1) + 15 min walk.
tips: From the tree, the tower is a 15-min taxi or Line 8 back to Jamsil.

options.title: Seoul Sky observatory
options.name: Seoul Sky
options.about: The observatory of Lotte World Tower — the world's fifth-tallest building — occupies floors 117–123, up to 500 m above the lake.
options.cool: Sky Deck glass floor on the 118th; café on the 123rd.
options.booking: Book the 16:45 slot online to skip the ticket queue.
tips: Go up 45 min before the 17:35 sunset and stay for the lights.

options.title: Seoul Sky + Sky Bridge Tour
options.name: Seoul Sky Bridge Tour
options.about: A harnessed walk across the open-air bridge between the tower's two spires at 541 m — the highest building bridge in the world — then the observatory.
options.cool: Only a handful of slots a day; you get the photos and a certificate.
options.booking: Book well ahead on the Seoul Sky site; weather-dependent, refunds if cancelled.
tips: Splurge option — it's ≈€60 each; the standard observatory is ₩31k.
No loose items on the bridge; phones go in a provided case.

options.title: Geumgeum, Songridan-gil
options.type: Korean bistro · rice bowls & small plates
options.name: 금금 송리단길
options.about: A cosy neighbourhood spot in the low-rise lanes east of Seokchon Lake — Songridan-gil is Seoul's answer to Tokyo's back alleys, full of small kitchens and wine bars.
options.cool: Ten-minute walk from the tower; the whole street is worth a wander after.
options.booking: Walk in; check the Naver page for today's menu and hours.
tips: Line 2 back to Konkuk Univ., 4 stops.

options.title: Konkuk lamb-skewer street
options.type: Chinese-Korean · lamb skewers grilled at the table
options.name: 건대 양꼬치거리
options.about: Behind Konkuk Univ. station, a whole street of yangkkochi houses: cumin-dusted lamb skewers turning on automatic grills, with Tsingtao and stir-fried lotus root.
options.cool: Loud, cheap, student energy — and it's next to your hotel.
tips: 10 skewers (≈₩15k) + one fried dish between two is plenty.
Konkuk Univ. station exit 5, 3 min.
